purpose: For each Store A product, retrieve a small high-recall set of Store B candidates. This module must NOT decide whether a pair is a match.

core_objective.hard_rule: Never reject a candidate solely because brand, size, category, flavor, or another attribute is missing or different.

important_data_constraints: Top-level category, department, subcategory, name_clean, and size_raw are empty in both datasets.
Useful taxonomy is embedded inside item_info.category_0..category_3.
A and B taxonomies are not directly aligned; exact category equality is forbidden as a retrieval gate.
A has much weaker brand, description, tag, and explicit-size coverage than B.
Store A includes grocery and many non-grocery departments; retrieval must be category-adaptive.

text: create both punctuation-stripped and character-preserving forms

derived_fields.name: title_norm
derived_fields.description: Normalized full title with informative numbers preserved.

derived_fields.name: brand_norm
derived_fields.description: Normalized observed brand. Name-based inference is allowed only as a retrieval hint, never as truth.

derived_fields.name: size_signature
derived_fields.description: Normalized quantity/unit/count/dimensions. Name extraction fills missing structured size.

derived_fields.name: numeric_signature
derived_fields.description: Numbers tied to units, percentages, dimensions, strengths, shade/model/spec codes.

derived_fields.name: core_product_tokens
derived_fields.description: Title tokens after removing brand, size/count tokens, and low-information marketing language.

derived_fields.name: modifier_tokens
derived_fields.description: Flavor, form, state, scent, color/shade, diet, material, life-stage and similar variant terms.

derived_fields.name: rare_tokens
derived_fields.description: High-IDF B-corpus tokens retained for discriminative retrieval.

indexing_strategy.implementation_note: Use sparse top-K similarity, not a dense A×B similarity matrix. Process A in batches and keep only per-query top-K results.

channels.name: exact_normalized_title
channels.goal: Catch same-product listings whose titles normalize identically.
channels.protected_candidate_rule: retain every exact-title hit through fusion
channels.why_separate: Provides a near-free high-signal route without making an automatic match decision.

channels.name: word_tfidf_title
channels.goal: Retrieve products sharing important words and short phrases.

channels.name: character_ngram_title
channels.goal: Survive spelling, punctuation, tokenization, pluralization, and formatting differences.

channels.name: core_product_lexical
channels.goal: Emphasize what the product is after stripping brand, quantity, and marketing noise.

channels.name: brand_augmented_lexical
channels.goal: Improve national-brand exact-product retrieval without excluding private-label equivalents.
channels.method: lexical score plus soft brand bonus
channels.activation: when brand is observed or confidently inferable

channels.name: taxonomy_augmented
channels.goal: Use product-family context to rescue ambiguous generic titles.
channels.method: lexical retrieval with soft taxonomy-token boost
channels.forbidden_behavior: Never require Store A and Store B category strings to match.
channels.reason: Observed taxonomies are structurally different and A contains noisy seasonal paths.

channels.name: quantity_pack_aware
channels.goal: Prefer same product with compatible quantity, pack count, or dimensions while retaining size-mismatch candidates.
channels.method: core lexical score plus soft normalized-size bonus
channels.forbidden_behavior: Never exclude because one side has missing or conflicting size.

channels.name: numeric_spec_code
channels.goal: Retrieve products distinguished by strengths, dimensions, shade numbers, model/spec codes, percentages, or pack counts.
channels.method: inverted lookup + IDF-weighted numeric/spec overlap + lexical tie-break
channels.protected_candidate_rule: Protect exact matches on strong alphanumeric/model/spec tokens; ordinary quantities such as 12 oz are not protected by themselves.

channels.name: rare_token_signature
channels.goal: Exploit uncommon product words that are highly discriminative.
channels.method: B-corpus inverted index ranked by sum(IDF(shared_rare_token))
channels.protected_candidate_rule: Protect candidates sharing >=2 independently rare tokens.

channels.name: variant_form_state
channels.goal: Retrieve the correct flavor/form/state/style variant when generic product terms are common.
channels.method: lexical retrieval with modifier overlap bonus
channels.forbidden_behavior: Do not exclude candidates with missing/different modifiers; contradiction belongs downstream.

channels.name: weighted_multifield_sparse
channels.goal: Use all available evidence while preventing B's rich descriptions from overpowering A's sparse records.
channels.method: field-specific sparse cosine scores combined by weighted sum
channels.note: Weights are deliberately conservative for description/tags because A coverage is weak.

channels.name: gpt5_nano_canonical_rescue
channels.goal: Recover candidates for noisy, underspecified, or cross-wording products that sparse channels do not agree on.

trigger_if_any: fewer than 12 unique candidates from R01-R11
no candidate appears in at least 2 independent channels
top fused candidate score is below the calibrated retrieval floor
title appears heavily marketing-dominated or structurally ambiguous

llm_task.instruction_boundary: GPT only rewrites/extracts retrieval queries. It does not decide MATCH/NON_MATCH and does not inspect the whole B dataset.

channels.search_method_after_llm: run generated canonical queries through R02/R04/R08/R09/R10 indexes

fusion_and_deduplication.step_1: Run R01-R11 and union candidate item_id_B values.
fusion_and_deduplication.step_2: Deduplicate by item_id_B while preserving each channel rank and raw score.
fusion_and_deduplication.step_3: Fuse ranks using weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
fusion_and_deduplication.step_4: Evaluate R12 only when its rescue triggers fire; merge its candidates and recompute fusion.
fusion_and_deduplication.step_5: Retain top 60 fused candidates plus protected candidates.
fusion_and_deduplication.important: Fusion weights are initialization values, not final learned/calibrated constants.

non_goals_and_forbidden_rules: Candidate retrieval never outputs MATCH or NON_MATCH.
Missing data is never treated as disagreement.
A candidate can survive because one strong independent channel found it.
Do not use GPT confidence as candidate truth.

evaluation_protocol.gold_set_requirement: Create a human-verified positive correspondence set before tuning. Use development/calibration/final-holdout splits.
evaluation_protocol.ablation_tests: Remove one channel at a time and measure lost positive correspondences. A channel stays only if it improves recall, robustness, or efficiency on a defined slice.
evaluation_protocol.no_test_leakage: Final holdout labels must not be used to tune channel weights, top_k, thresholds, or rescue triggers.

efficiency_budget.principle: Spend cheap sparse/inverted-index work to protect recall; reserve GPT and 140-attribute adjudication for the small candidate set.

planned_tuning_order: Enable R12 only for observed failure modes.
Tune per-channel top_k and fusion weights on development/calibration data.
Evaluate once on untouched final holdout.
Only then feed candidates into Match Engine.
